info.name: retailcloud Catalog Service API - QA Gap Coverage
info.description:
Targets the specific coverage gaps identified in the CRUD collection review: negative/validation testing, multi-tenant isolation, guarded referential-integrity deactivation, Department merge validation, batch update atomic vs best-effort behavior, Recipe versioning invariants, expand-gated reads, Modifier<->Item association endpoints, search/filter/pagination edge cases, response-contract and read-only-field checks, immutable fields, concurrency/idempotency, and data boundary/encoding cases.

Setup:
1. Set `base_url` and `access_token` (Tenant A).
2. Set `access_token_tenant_b` to a bearer token for a DIFFERENT merchant/domain — required only by folder 02 (Multi-Tenant Isolation); every other folder uses `access_token` alone.
3. Run folders top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner. Each folder is self-contained and creates whatever setup data it needs via {{$randomInt}}-suffixed names, so folders can be re-run without colliding with previous runs (with the exception of folder 01's two hard-coded 'Gluten'/'gluten' duplicate-name checks and folder 12's hard-coded duplicate-create check, which are intentionally static to test the uniqueness constraint — delete/reset those records between runs, or expect the 'create' half to 409 on a second run).

Where the spec doesn't explicitly document the expected outcome, the test asserts the range of defensible outcomes (e.g. `pm.expect([200, 400]).to.include(...)`) and logs the actual status/body to the console — treat those as 'confirm and tighten this assertion once you know the intended behavior' rather than a definitive pass/fail.

item.name: 06 - Recipe Versioning Rules
Create Recipe with TWO active versions -> expect rejection or auto-correction

request.description: This is an ambiguous-by-spec case: does the API 400/409 the request, or silently keep only the last ACTIVE version? Either is defensible — the test logs the outcome for the team to confirm is intentional.

exec: pm.test("Spec says 'one ACTIVE version per recipe' — confirm which of reject vs auto-resolve actually happens", function () { pm.expect([400, 409, 201, 200]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
console.log("two active versions create -> actual status:", pm.response.code, pm.response.text().slice(0,300));

if (pm.response.code < 300) { try { var jsonData = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('two_active_recipe_id', jsonData.data.id); var actives = (jsonData.data.versions || []).filter(v => v.status === 'ACTIVE'); console.log('active version count on created recipe:', actives.length); pm.test('If accepted, server enforces a single active version', function () { pm.expect(actives.length).to.equal(1); }); } catch (e) {} }

item.name: Create Recipe with one ACTIVE + one DRAFT version -> 201

exec: pm.test("Status code is one of [201, 200]", function () { pm.expect([201, 200]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

if (pm.response.code < 300) { try { var jsonData = pm.response.json(); var val = jsonData.data.id; if (val !== undefined && val !== null) {  pm.collectionVariables.set("version_recipe_id", val);  console.log("Saved version_recipe_id =", val); } } catch (e) { console.log('could not capture version_recipe_id:', e); } }

exec: pm.test("Confirm whether a partial versions[] patch is even accepted for promotion", function () { pm.expect([200, 400]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
console.log("promote draft -> actual status:", pm.response.code, pm.response.text().slice(0,300));

item.name: Get Recipe - confirm exactly one ACTIVE version after promotion

exec: pm.test("Status code is one of [200]", function () { pm.expect([200]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

var jsonData = pm.response.json(); var actives = (jsonData.data.versions || []).filter(v => v.status === 'ACTIVE'); pm.test('Exactly one ACTIVE version', function () { pm.expect(actives.length).to.equal(1); }); pm.test('Version 2 is now the active one', function () { var v2 = (jsonData.data.versions||[]).find(v=>v.version===2); pm.expect(v2 && v2.status).to.eql('ACTIVE'); });

item.description: Recipe is documented as 'recipe -> versions -> lines... one ACTIVE version per recipe' with no separate /versions endpoint, so the invariant lives inside the single Recipe payload. Untested by the CRUD collection.

item.name: 10 - Response Contract & Read-Only Field Protection
